---
title: "Labor Productivity"
---

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all()
library(tidyverse)
library(zoo)
```

The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publishes quarterly labor productivity growth rates (% change from previous quarter) for major US economic sectors. We analyze five sectors:

- `DUR`: Durable manufacturing
- `NDUR`: Nondurable manufacturing
- `NFC`: Nonfinancial corporate
- `NFBUS`: Nonfarm business
- `BUS`: Business

Productivity growth is subject to structural breaks driven by recessions, policy changes, and technological shifts — making this a natural setting for ECE. We compare ECE against oracle segmentation, where change points are estimated from the data using `segment_mean()`.

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false

X_data <- read_csv(
  "~/Documents/Research/Code/ECE/data/real-data/bls-labor-productivity.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Reconstruct quarterly dates starting 1987 Q2
n <- nrow(X_data)
dates <- as.yearqtr("1987 Q2") + (0:(n - 1)) / 4

X_segment <- segment_mean(as.matrix(X_data), penalty = "Manual", pen.value = 0) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_segment"))

X <- bind_cols(date = dates, X_data, X_segment)
```

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-bls-productivity
#| fig-cap: "Quarterly labor productivity growth by sector. Thick lines show segmented means."

X |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -date, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    type   = if_else(str_ends(series, "_segment"), "Segmented", "Raw"),
    sector = str_remove(series, "_segment$")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = value, color = sector, group = series)) +
  geom_line(aes(linewidth = type)) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(Raw = 0.5, Segmented = 1.0), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Labor Productivity by Sector",
    x = "Date",
    y = "% Change from Previous Quarter",
    color = "Sector",
    caption = "Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{R}
#| echo: false

X_mat      <- as.matrix(X_data)
X_seg_mat  <- as.matrix(X_segment)

ece_cor         <- ece.cor(X_mat) |> round(3)
rownames(ece_cor) <- colnames(ece_cor) <- colnames(X_data)

segment_cor     <- cor(X_mat - X_seg_mat) |> round(3)
pearson_cor     <- cor(X_mat) |> round(3)

ece_pmat        <- ece_pval(X_mat) |> round(3)
segment_pmat    <- cor_pval(X_mat - X_seg_mat) |> round(3)
pearson_pmat    <- cor_pval(X_mat) |> round(3)
```
